channel.title: Paperraft
channel.description: Research in efficient inference and AI agents, ranked by independent GitHub implementations instead of citations or stars. Papers above the attention threshold are deliberately excluded.

item.title: Hidden Cartographer: Hidden State Guided Data Selection for Dual Budgeted Instruction Tuning
item.description: It replaces pseudo-label-based selection and conventional active learning with a two-stage process: progressive candidate expansion using a hidden-state proxy, then exact training-dynamics pruning to a compact fine-tuning subset. It costs repeated proxy updates and training-dynamics recomputation during the expansion loop, adding pipeline complexity and compute beyond a single-pass selection, though it reduces annotation and fine-tuning volume substantially. It can fail if the proxy's hidden-state signals mischaracterize which examples are valuable, or if domain-specific dynamics do not transfer, making validation on the reader's own data distribution necessary before relying on the reported accuracy advantage. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: efficient training. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Improving the Expressive Power of Hybrid Sequence Models via Multi-Hop Retrieval
item.description: MuRA replaces conventional hybrid blocks (full-attention layers plus fixed-state efficient layers) by letting efficient layers perform m sequential retrieval hops from a shared KV cache, which provably enables m-function composition where existing blocks require capacity scaling as Omega(sqrt(n)) even for two hops. The cost is architectural: it is a new block design that requires training from scratch or fine-tuning a custom implementation, with added implementation complexity in the retrieval mechanism, though it preserves asymptotic compute and memory efficiency. It can fail in practice because the evidence is a theoretical expressivity hierarchy plus synthetic composition tasks; there is no demonstration on pretrained models, real downstream benchmarks, or pretrained-checkpoint compatibility, so gains may not transfer to production workloads. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: efficient architectures. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: MOSAIC: Multi-Objective Search for Allocating Inference Cache Across LLM Decoder Layers
item.description: MOSAIC replaces uniform per-layer KV-cache budgets (as used by SnapKV, H2O, AdaKV, L2Norm-style eviction) with a per-layer budget allocation found by one multi-objective search whose best allocation transfers across target budgets, optionally refined by a budget-constrained search. The cost is a one-time offline search per model and eviction method (reported as cheaper than EvolKV, but still multi-evaluation GPU work on a single 24 GB card for 7-8B models), plus serving-side plumbing to track and enforce per-layer budgets, with no runtime quality loss claimed at matched budgets. It can fail if the searched allocation does not transfer to models, tasks, context lengths, or eviction methods outside the validated Llama-3-8B / Mistral-7B and RULER/LongBench settings, or if the serving stack cannot apply heterogeneous per-layer budgets without kernel or scheduler changes. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: KV cache. Recommendation: test.

item.title: System X: An LLM Decision Model That Replies from Its Own KV Cache
item.description: The method replaces a separate full-prompt second LLM call for text replies with continuation from the decision model's existing KV cache after a Jev-style option readout. It costs a LoRA fine-tuning pipeline, routing-data curation, and added serving complexity, and gains remain workload-dependent rather than a fixed multiplicative factor. Failures include state conflicts, unsupported reply details, possible instruction-following degradation from added support data, and reply-judge results confounded by prompt and generation-limit differences. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: KV cache. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Reliability-Preserving Compression for Deployable Medical Image Segmentation
item.description: SGAV-MP replaces uniform post-training quantization, pruning, or distillation pipelines that select layer precisions by Dice and size alone, by scoring quantization actions on a benefit-risk basis and accepting them only after full-model reliability validation on a calibration set. The cost is an added calibration and validation stage per quantization candidate, plus reliance on a backend such as TensorRT to convert stored compression into actual runtime speedup, which the paper reports separately. It can fail if the calibration set is unrepresentative of deployment data, in which case the accepted precision assignments may preserve uncertainty agreement in validation but not in production, and the method is validated only on MRI/CT segmentation, so transfer to other tasks is unverified. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: quantization. Recommendation: test.

item.title: StreamAhead: Real-Time Streaming Video Question Answering via Adaptive Precomputation
item.description: StreamAhead replaces the standard practice of building full KV caches for every incoming video segment with a tiered scheme that keeps segments at cheap representation levels (visual features) and materializes KV caches only for query-retrieved segments. The cost is an offline profiling step per segment and model, a runtime scheduler that pipelines segment computation across CPU and GPU concurrently with queries, and the query-time compute of completing KV caches for retrieved segments. It can fail when the retrieval stage selects the wrong segments, when query arrival bursts exceed the scheduler's ability to complete KV caches within latency targets, or when the offline cost profiles do not transfer to the deployment hardware or model. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: serving and batching. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Adversarial Post-Training of Foundation Models for High-Frequency Trading
item.description: The method replaces additional cross-entropy pre-training of a limit-order-book generator with a short adversarial post-training stage: a WGAN critic evaluates free-running rollouts through the real matching engine and evolution strategies update rank-4 LoRA perturbations under a KL trust region. It costs under 50M training tokens and roughly 12 GPU-hours per seed, but presupposes an existing pre-trained LOB foundation model (a 48B-token pre-training budget), access to a non-differentiable matching engine, and online critic infrastructure. It can fail through reward hacking of the critic, as the paper's own analysis notes, and its gains are specific to market-simulation fidelity rather than general language-model quality. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: efficient training. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: LOOP: Recovery-Aligned Iterative Layer Pruning via On-Policy Distillation
item.description: Replaces one-shot layer pruning followed by a single recovery phase with an iterative loop that removes one layer at a time, runs short on-policy distillation after each removal, and reuses recovery signals to select subsequent layers. Costs repeated distillation cycles with on-policy trajectory generation (teacher rollouts at every shot), which raises compute and wall-clock budget well beyond a one-shot prune, though it preserves a dense architecture that runs on standard hardware after pruning. Can fail if the per-shot recovery budget is insufficient to make the pruning signal informative, if on-policy distillation is unstable for the target model, or if the accuracy gains over cheaper one-shot baselines do not justify the added training cost on a limited budget. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: sparsity and pruning. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Corrected Block Sparse Spectral Optimization: Exact Models, Finite Identification, and Local Dynamics
item.description: Replaces dense PCA and the ambiguous standard block generalized-power sparse-PCA formulation with a primal-derived soft-threshold objective (A-SQ), a safeguarded Riemannian ascent with proven convergence, finite support identification, and post-identification refitting via power iteration. Cost is modest: Stiefel updates and thresholding on covariance-scale data run on a single GPU or CPU, with added implementation complexity for tie-breaking, zero-response columns, and mask-before-refit conventions. It can fail when the strict threshold-margin assumption does not hold, delaying or preventing support identification, and the quality gains are dataset-specific additive AMI improvements rather than guaranteed uplifts on arbitrary workloads. 1 independent implementation, 0 stars. Research area: sparsity and pruning. Recommendation: test.

item.title: How Much Does One Wrong Answer Cost? Error Propagation in Constraint Pruning with Noisy LLM Oracles
item.description: The method does not replace constraint pruning itself; it replaces the assumption that a correct oracle makes query order irrelevant, prescribing query orders (notably pivot orders for entity resolution) that bound how far one wrong LLM answer propagates. It costs nothing in extra queries or infrastructure, only deliberate ordering of the same yes/no questions, with pivot ordering being simple to implement. It can fail when error independence or small-epsilon assumptions break down (correlated oracle errors, systematic biases toward certain record pairs), since the guarantees are first-order in epsilon and the common most-similar-first ordering is provably the worst in one dimension. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: failure recovery. Recommendation: test.

item.title: The KV-Surgeon: Compensation-Aware Offline KV-Cache Compaction
item.description: Replaces per-entry independent scoring for KV-cache eviction (e.g., attention matching) with a calibration-data-driven quadratic surrogate that jointly selects removals and compensates remaining entries, accounting for softmax renormalization. Cost is a one-time offline compaction pass with calibration data per fixed context, plus the memory of retaining a small calibration set; the compacted cache then reduces per-query memory and compute on repeated queries. It can fail when the queried context is not fixed and reused (no amortization of the offline cost), when calibration data is unrepresentative of production queries, or when compaction ratios are pushed beyond the validated operating points. 2 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: KV cache. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Latent Projection for Latent Planning
item.description: The method replaces the raw l2 distance between predicted and goal latents with an l2 distance restricted to the k-dimensional subspace that the learned state dynamics propagate with least uncertainty, derived from a normal-matrix transition model fit under SIGReg regularization. The cost is fitting a single constrained matrix A post hoc; the encoder, predictor, rollout, and planner remain unchanged, adding negligible compute. The approach can fail if the SIGReg and Gauss-Markov assumptions do not hold for the reader's environment, if the latent dynamics are not well-approximated by a normal linear map, and the reported gains are demonstrated only on 2D navigation tasks, so transfer to other domains is unvalidated. 1 independent implementation, 1 star. Research area: planning and decomposition. Recommendation: test.

item.title: ORBIT: Autoregressive Time Series Generation via Next Frequency-Band Prediction
item.description: ORBIT replaces conventional time-series generative models (GANs, diffusion models, and standard autoregressive transformers) with a two-stage framework: a Frequency-Hierarchical VQ-VAE that decomposes latent representations into frequency bands with residual quantization, and a Frequency-Band Autoregressive Transformer that generates from low to high frequencies. The abstract claims state-of-the-art overall performance and superior inference efficiency compared with advanced baselines, but provides no quantitative factor in the abstract itself; assessing actual compute and memory costs requires consulting the full paper. The approach demands training both a custom VQ-VAE and a custom transformer on the reader's own time-series data, which adds implementation complexity and training time; it can fail if the reader lacks sufficient domain-specific training data, if the frequency decomposition does not match the characteristics of the target signals, or if the claimed efficiency gains do not materialize at the reader's data scale and sequence lengths. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: efficient architectures. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Robust Latent Variable Graphical Models: Exact Recovery and Fundamental Limits
item.description: The method replaces the sample covariance in sparse-plus-low-rank precision matrix estimation with a centered Gaussian measure-transformed covariance, penalizing the low-rank component via a nuclear norm of a congruence transform. It costs a convex optimization solved by a linearized ADMM with closed-form updates, with statistical guarantees requiring N greater than roughly p/nu_min^2 samples for inertia recovery and restricted invertibility plus irrepresentability conditions on the Fisher information. Signed-graph and inertia recovery can fail when these structural conditions are violated, when the low-rank eigenvalues are too small relative to sample size, or under Huber contamination beyond the quantified bias bound, though the bound vanishes for remote outliers. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: Decomposed Relation Extraction from Aviation Accident Narratives: Evaluating Transformer-Based Safety Knowledge Discovery under Relational Sparsity
item.description: The method replaces end-to-end relation extraction with a decomposed pipeline: candidate concept pairs are enumerated first, then a TF-IDF Linear SVM or weighted RoBERTa classifier labels them as RESULTS_IN or CONTRIBUTES_TO. Cost is dominated by the candidate space (21,038 pairs from 300 narratives) and by quality: exhaustive evaluation collapsed Macro-F1 from ~0.47-0.48 in development to 0.24-0.27, with MCC near zero (0.013-0.020) and 7,018-9,824 false positives against 96-125 recovered true relations. What fails after adoption is precision at deployment scale: hard-negative sampled development scores did not transfer to exhaustive candidate evaluation, RoBERTa confidence distributions overlapped between classes, and false positives persisted even within valid relation directions, so known concept endpoints do not yield reliable extraction. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: retrieval and RAG. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: MultiCard: Multiple Attribute Cardinality Estimation via Deep Learning
item.description: MultiCard replaces PostgreSQL's default cardinality estimator and prior single-predicate learned estimators (histograms, LIKE-only or range-only models) with a single end-to-end neural model combining a Transformer, an LSTM, a numerical histogram encoder, and a predicate-interaction Transformer, trained on labeled queries. The cost is a supervised training pipeline requiring exact cardinality labels (produced by the UPCI workload generator), model maintenance as data and schema drift, and integration work with the query optimizer, plus small GPU or CPU inference overhead per query. It can fail on schema or data distributions not covered by the training workload, since learned estimators degrade under drift and the reported gains hold only on the five evaluated datasets and generated workloads. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Discrete Neural Interlingua for Ontology-Agnostic EHR Modeling
item.description: MEDIATOR replaces fixed-vocabulary EHR tokenizers and manual ontology crosswalks with a vector-quantized tokenizer that maps any clinical concept text into a shared discrete codebook, enabling cross-hospital transfer without hand-built mappings. Adoption costs training the tokenizer with synonym supervision plus co-occurrence and relation-graph objectives, and integrating it as the input layer of a downstream EHR Transformer rather than a drop-in inference component. It can fail where source systems lack usable concept text (codes without descriptions), where the learned codebook collapses genuinely distinct concepts, or where evaluation is confined to a single hospital because the reported gains concentrate on cross-institution transfer. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Reconstruction-Optimized Expert Pruning for Mixture-of-Experts Language Models
item.description: OptEP replaces heuristic or search-based expert-pruning criteria with a continuous relaxation that optimizes differentiable expert-selection variables against a reconstruction objective, followed by a lightweight update of retained expert weights; the pruned experts are removed, reducing storage and deployment memory for MoE models. Cost is a post-training calibration procedure requiring task-domain data, per-layer reconstruction optimization, and the weight-adaptation pass, plus some residual accuracy loss relative to the unpruned model. It can fail when calibration data is not representative of production traffic, when pruning is pushed to ratios the reconstruction objective cannot compensate for, and on hardware or serving stacks where sparse expert routing gives no realized speed or memory benefit despite fewer stored experts. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: sparsity and pruning. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Sustainable Processing-in-DRAM Integration and Replacement for Transformer Inference Servers
item.description: The paper evaluates replacing or augmenting GPU inference servers with Processing-in-DRAM (PID) accelerators, providing a carbon modeling framework covering embodied, idle, and active carbon plus an aging-aware replacement schedule over 10 years. Adoption costs are substantial: PID hardware is not commercially procurable for a small team, requires server-level integration paired with specific GPUs, and results depend strongly on GPU pairing, with HGX-H100 servers showing 5.4-5.9x higher total carbon than A100/H100 configurations. The findings can fail in practice because they are model-based projections rather than measurements from deployed PID systems, and the optimal replacement period depends on carbon-intensity assumptions and workload mix. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: How Far Can the Gemma 4 Speech Encoder Go Without Changing Its Weights? Saudi and Gulf Arabic Speech Recognition with a Frozen and an Adapter-Augmented Encoder
item.description: The method replaces full fine-tuning of a speech foundation model (or reliance on a commercial ASR API) with a frozen pretrained encoder plus a small trainable CTC or hybrid CTC/attention reader and optional low-rank adapters, targeting Arabic dialect ASR. It costs training and validation effort on domain data (around 25.7M to 44.6M trainable parameters), still trails the commercial baseline in WER on long-form speech, and adds pipeline complexity in layer mixing and joint decoding. It can fail on domains far from the Saudi/Gulf data used, and the paper itself warns that human-corrected machine drafts bias evaluation toward the drafting system. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: efficient training. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Mitigating Reward Hacking in Realistic Scenarios Through Representation Engineering
item.description: The method replaces prompt-level anti-reward-hacking instructions and output-only monitors with activation-space monitoring plus dynamic steering-vector interventions on the residual stream, including for tool calls and long contexts. Costs include labeled or otherwise sourced rollouts for vector extraction, additional inference-time intervention machinery, and potential small degradation in coherence or capability if steering is miscalibrated. It can fail when extracted vectors do not transfer to the production distribution, when activation monitoring misses novel hacking strategies, or when interventions suppress undesirable behavior only partially while affecting useful behavior. 1 independent implementation, 3 stars. Research area: safety and guardrails. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Steering Black-Box Large Language Model Agents with Pitfall Anticipation World Model
item.description: PAWM replaces per-step next-observation world models with a selectively invoked model that predicts impending multi-step failures and steers a black-box LLM agent away from them. It costs a two-stage training pipeline: supervised fine-tuning on synthetic pitfall-labeled data plus GRPO co-training against the target environment, plus added inference latency at intervention points. It can fail when the synthetic pitfall distribution mismatches the deployment environment, when pitfalls are mispredicted (false interventions can derail correct trajectories), and the method requires retraining per environment. 1 independent implementation, 218 stars. Research area: planning and decomposition. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: VeeReview: Measuring Build-Verify Pairs in Agent-Authored Pull Requests from a V-Model Perspective
item.description: VeeReview replaces informal human judgement of whether a pull request's verification evidence matches its proposed change with a hybrid of deterministic repository signals, one rule over the diff and tree, and a language-model judge for the remaining pairs. The cost is building repository-signal extraction plus LLM judging per pull request, and the authors themselves show the instrument did not meet its calibration target: agreement with adjudicated labels was only 4% to 60% against a required 80%, and inter-rater agreement was weak (kappa = 0.154). What can fail is exactly what the paper demonstrates: the model-judged pairs partly measure how a pull request is presented rather than the verification work performed, so adopting it for gating or comparing agent versus human output would encode an unvalidated measurement. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: TeachBack: Learning to Teach via Bidirectional Preference Optimization for On-Policy Self-Distillation
item.description: TeachBack replaces standard on-policy self-distillation where the Teacher has static privileged access to the solution with a bidirectional preference-learning framework that shapes the Teacher's generation via reference-length control and prompt variation. It requires generating paired privileged and non-privileged trajectories at each rollout refresh and optimizing a pairwise preference objective, which increases training compute and implementation complexity compared to standard OPSD. The method can fail if the privileged Teacher trajectories, despite accuracy, omit the exploration and self-correction behaviors necessary for the Student to learn robust problem-solving without privileged information. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: distillation. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: ExpEvolve: Structuring and Reusing Experience for Open-Ended Discovery
item.description: Replaces surface-level mutation heuristics in evolutionary coding agents (e.g., AlphaEvolve-style loops) with extracted high-level 'idea factors' that explain score differences and guide exploitation and plateau-breaking exploration. Costs additional LLM calls for factor extraction and control plus a persistent experience store, adding orchestration complexity on top of an already compute-heavy evolutionary search. Can fail if the extracted factors do not capture true causal drivers of score differences, if the task lacks a cheap reliable scorer, or if the API-call budget makes multi-round evolution prohibitively expensive. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: coding agents. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Signals and Queries: Token-Efficient Agentic Context Discovery
item.description: S&Q replaces per-turn LLM-based relevance evaluation of every behavioral policy with an offline-trained, per-policy logistic classifier over embeddings that filters candidates before any LLM call. The cost is an offline generation step (activating examples and hard negatives per policy), classifier training and maintenance per policy, and a small risk of false negatives that downstream stages never see. It can fail when user behavior drifts from the offline training examples, when new policies lack sufficient generated examples, or when embedding quality is poor for the domain, since a wrongly discarded policy is silently excluded from that turn. 2 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: memory and context. Recommendation: adopt.

item.title: Seeing the Forest for the Trees: Emergent Agreement from Individual Conversations
item.description: This is an interpretability and analysis method, not a production component: it replaces ad hoc monitoring of multi-agent agreement with linear probes on activations plus cross-conversation aggregation and a Markov model of turn-level agreement. The cost is the instrumentation itself: activation capture, probe training, and aggregation infrastructure, with no claimed gain in speed, memory, cost, or task quality. It can fail for deployment purposes because the per-conversation internal signal is explicitly unreliable, and the findings are descriptive of model behavior rather than a mechanism for controlling or improving it. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: multi-agent orchestration. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: AgentMonopoly: Behavioral Patterns and Persona Control in LLM Agents
item.description: AgentMonopoly replaces ad-hoc or purely linguistic evaluation of LLM agent personas with an open-source Monopoly-style environment that measures persona adherence through actions and outcomes over multi-turn games. Adoption costs engineering effort to set up and run the environment, plus API inference costs for repeated games across models and seeds, with no reduction in production serving cost or latency. It can fail to transfer because the findings are conditional on the tested checkpoints, prompts, and only five seeds per configuration, so persona control observed in the game may not hold in the reader's production tasks. 0 independent implementations, 122 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Do Coding Agents Understand Why Systems Crash---and Why They Don't?
item.description: The method replaces single-version crash prediction benchmarks with paired source trees differing by one commit, so a correct-looking prediction on crashing code alone is no longer accepted as evidence of execution reasoning. It costs the construction of matched pre/post-commit tree pairs with a verified crash-triggering input (934 pairs here from Linux and OSS-Fuzz), plus roughly double the agent evaluation runs per case. It can fail if pairs are not truly minimal, if the crash input is flaky, or if agents refuse or time out on large systems codebases, and it measures crash reasoning only, not general bug-fixing ability. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: test.

item.title: DynaWeave: Learning to Adapt through Dynamic Scenario Synthesis
item.description: Replaces static task environments with dynamically synthesized scenarios where exogenous events (requirement changes, state shifts, external information updates) activate during agent interaction via DAG-based dependency graphs and an execution engine. Costs include building the synthesis framework, generating and verifying 2,095 trajectories across 36 environments, and supervised fine-tuning of Qwen3.5 models, requiring non-trivial engineering and compute. Can fail if synthesized events do not match production event distributions, if the dynamic verifier introduces evaluation errors, or if fine-tuned models overfit to synthetic dynamics rather than genuine adaptation. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: efficient training. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Bridging Foundational and Agentic Capabilities of LLMs
item.description: The method replaces end-to-end agent benchmark scoring with a dual-profile framework that compares foundational capability benchmarks against operation-level interaction trajectories to locate execution failures. It costs the effort of collecting and annotating interaction trajectories plus fitting predictive mappings, which is feasible on a limited budget but adds evaluation engineering overhead. It can fail if the τ²-Bench-derived operation taxonomy does not transfer to the reader's production task distribution, or if foundational benchmarks mismeasure the capabilities actually exercised by the deployment. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: test.

item.title: UserSWE: Evaluating Coding Agents in Multi-Turn Conversations with Dynamic Users
item.description: UserSWE replaces single-turn issue-report benchmarks with multi-turn coding tasks in which a persona-driven simulated user reveals information progressively and execution-grounded tests gate verdicts after every turn. Adopting it costs the construction or reuse of its task pipeline plus API or compute spend for running agents, the simulated user, and the dual-family verdict agents across up to eight turns per task. It can fail to transfer to a specific production setting because the 72 tasks and 42 repositories may not match the reader's codebase, and simulated-user behavior calibrated on past sessions may diverge from real user interactions. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: test.

item.title: PAUSE: Search-Free Steering of Coding Agents Before Their First Source-Code Edit
item.description: PAUSE replaces periodic trajectory reviews, learned monitors, and search-over-checkpoints steering with one intervention: the agent's first source-code edit is intercepted, a separate Planner model writes a repair plan from the pre-edit transcript, and the same agent resumes with its context and workspace intact. The cost is one extra Planner call per run (a strong frontier model such as GPT-5.6 Sol in the reported results), plus engineering to hook the edit tool in the agent harness; Executor compute is unchanged and offline replay saves 33-41% of Executor tokens versus restarting. It can fail when the Planner is weaker than the Executor's own reasoning, when the task's decisive error occurs after the first edit and is never revisited, or when the harness cannot expose a clean pre-edit interception point. 2 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: coding agents. Recommendation: test.

item.title: ToM2Vec: Continuous Theory-of-Mind Tokens for Multi-Agent Coordination
item.description: ToM2Vec replaces explicit text-based reasoning about partner states with a fixed budget of continuous latent tokens trained to abstract a partner's thoughts. It costs the complexity of a specialized training phase supervised by partner thoughts and requires managing a latent conditioning mechanism that is less inspectable than text. A failure mode is that performance degrades if this latent reasoning is forced into text, and the abstract nature of the tokens could obscure errors in the agent's model of its partners. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: multi-agent orchestration. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Agent Behavior Maps: Locating Agents by What They Would Do, Without Running Them
item.description: The method replaces direct environment rollouts for comparing and predicting LLM agent behavior: instead of running each agent-harness combination in the environment, it cross-scores centered action log-likelihoods on shared reference trajectories to build a behavioral coordinate map. The cost is maintaining a set of reference trajectories, running one inference pass per candidate model over them, and accepting that trajectory-KL correspondence holds only under the paper's explicit assumptions, with the harness-composition extension showing accuracy varying across components and environments. It can fail when reference trajectories are unrepresentative of the deployment task distribution, when scoring diverges from actual rollout behavior for out-of-family models or novel harnesses, or when rank-order agreement with KL does not translate into accurate absolute performance prediction. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: test.

item.title: HGM-Dual: Lineage-Aware Guided Agent Harness Optimization for Long-Horizon Planning
item.description: HGM-Dual replaces unstructured agent archives and purely open-ended self-modification with lineage-aware evolution context plus dual-path child generation that targets likely constraint-violating harness components. It costs extra bookkeeping of ancestor edits, failure attribution, and multiple child evaluations per parent, so implementation complexity is nontrivial even though the base LLM can remain frozen or API-based. It can fail if constraint diagnostics are wrong, lineage records attribute improvements incorrectly, or planning tasks do not show stable constraint-violation patterns for specialized edits to exploit. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: planning and decomposition. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: SWE-DIVE: Multi-Turn Coding Agent Evaluation with Dynamic User Simulation
item.description: SWE-DIVE replaces static, one-shot GitHub-issue benchmarks (e.g., SWE-bench) with dynamic, multi-turn user simulation to evaluate coding agents. It introduces complexity by requiring a user simulator, conversation validator, and orchestration environment (Harbor), which increases setup overhead and evaluation cost compared to single-turn benchmarks. Potential failure modes include unrealistic user behavior simulation, validator misalignment with true task requirements, and high infrastructure demands for continuous orchestration that may exceed constrained budgets. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Quant-Arena: Benchmarking LLM Agents for Quantitative Trading Research
item.description: Quant-Arena replaces ad-hoc evaluation of trading agents with a sealed backtest that forces models to generate features, signals, and code under realistic trading constraints. It costs access to proprietary A-share data, a backtesting engine, and LLM usage, and adds complexity via feature engineering and signal-code generation. The sealed 2024 test shows no frontier model beats the equal-weight market, so there is no production edge to adopt and the approach can fail after deployment. 2 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: Feedback That Backfires in Games: Do LLM Players Repeat the Move They Just Watched Fail?
item.description: Replaces the common harness pattern of appending the failed action and error message verbatim into the transcript before retrying; use a failure description that omits the move string, or at minimum decoder-level bans on exact repeats. Costs nothing in memory, latency, or infrastructure, though it requires careful prompt/harness design and omits information the model might in principle use. What can fail: the effect is model-dependent (present in base models, largely removed at the DPO stage), a 'do not repeat' instruction does nothing, and decoder bans stop exact repeats but not other illegal moves, so illegal play can persist. 1 independent implementation, 126 stars. Research area: failure recovery. Recommendation: adopt.

item.title: SWE-VERIFIER: Selective Verification for Cost-Efficient Coding Agents
item.description: Replaces always-on candidate sampling and per-step verification (or unverified single-action execution) with a lightweight 4B verifier that triggers sampling only on low-confidence steps and ranks candidate actions before execution. Costs training a small verifier model plus a modest inference overhead of roughly 1.1x API cost, and adds a preference-data training pipeline as integration complexity. Can fail if the verifier miscalibrates on out-of-distribution agent policies or task types, since gains are demonstrated only on the mini-swe-agent harness with two specific models and generalization to other agents is not guaranteed. 3 independent implementations, 34 stars. Research area: coding agents. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Trail-Weighted Influence Scores for Approximate Outcome Prediction in Bayesian Networks
item.description: The method replaces full-evidence exact inference in Bayesian networks with posterior computation over a pruned evidence set selected by trail-score thresholding. It costs a trail-enumeration and scoring pass whose runtime exceeds the inference it saves on most benchmark networks, and it carries no error guarantee outside collider-free binary trees with dropped trails on separate branches. It fails when dropped trails share a branch of the outcome node, and the proven bound does not extend to networks with colliders or loops. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: DStill: Trajectory Consistency Distillation for Accelerated One-Step Drafting in Block Diffusion Speculative Decoding
item.description: The method replaces iterative multi-step refinement in block-diffusion speculative drafting with a distilled one-step student trained on the drafter's own refinement trajectories. It requires a two-stage training pipeline, curriculum from partially revealed to fully masked blocks, and access to a block-diffusion drafter compatible with the target model family. It can fail if the one-step student retains token factorization errors on out-of-distribution prompts or if acceptance length degrades on tasks underrepresented in the trajectory curriculum. 2 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: speculative decoding. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Steering intonational tunes in text-to-speech synthesis
item.description: The method replaces prompt-based intonation control (which the paper shows mostly fails except for final punctuation) with difference-of-means steering vectors applied to the transformer backbone's hidden state during generation in RVQ-based TTS systems such as CSM and S2. It costs a small drop in predicted naturalness, requires collecting human imitations of the target tunes to compute vectors, and adds per-step intervention logic inside the generation loop; punctuation-derived vectors are simpler but degrade the voice when pushing toward assertions. It can fail to select a precise target tune beyond a broad falling or rising tendency, and the pitch accent may not follow the edge tone, so utterance-level intonation may remain internally inconsistent. 1 independent implementation, 673 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Building a Nested LADDER for LLM Unstructured Post-Training Pruning
item.description: It replaces uniform or heuristic layer-wise sparsity allocation in post-training pruning (e.g., standard SparseGPT allocation) with a greedy procedure that, at each step, commits the layer update causing the least end-to-end degradation per removed parameter, producing exactly nested masks across budgets. The cost is added pruning-time computation—repeated candidate evaluations across layers at every sparsity step—plus integration complexity on top of a backend such as SparseGPT; inference cost of the pruned model is unchanged. It can fail at benign sparsity (10-60%), where it is comparable or slightly weaker than baselines, and the high-sparsity benefit did not survive distillation on one of five models. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: sparsity and pruning. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Extreme Low-State Quantized Transformer for Electricity-Load Forecasting
item.description: The method replaces full-precision weights in a Transformer forecaster with 3-, 5-, 7-, or 16-state quantized weights, trained via quantization-aware fine-tuning or scratch QAT, plus an accumulated-update thresholding scheme that suppresses weight-state activity. The cost is a residual forecasting-accuracy penalty (direct PTQ adds 6.25–7.04 NRMSE points, of which QAT-FT recovers roughly 90–95%), additional training complexity, and a custom quantization pipeline rather than off-the-shelf INT8 deployment. It can fail because results are demonstrated only on two electricity-load datasets with small sequence models, the targets are multilevel synaptic edge devices that are not commercially available, and no standard GPU latency or memory benchmarks are reported, so gains may not transfer to the reader's 24 GB GPU inference workloads. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: quantization. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Engineering Low-Latency, High-Throughput Quantum Decoders on NVIDIA GPUs
item.description: The method replaces CPU-based or unoptimized GPU quantum error correction decoders with a CUDA-Graph-driven Relay belief-propagation decoder using mixed FP16-FP32 arithmetic, INT8 quantization, and concurrent decoder instances. It costs substantial CUDA engineering effort, quantization accuracy risk mitigated by higher-precision accumulators, and workload-specific tuning per code family. It can fail if quantization degrades logical error rates on untested codes or error regimes, and it is irrelevant unless the adopter operates quantum error correction workloads. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: Amplified Pruning and Path Selectors for Deterministic Radio Gossiping
item.description: The method replaces prior deterministic radio-network gossip protocols based on Wu and Chrobak-style path selection with amplified reception certificates, adaptive pruning, and permutation selectors. Its cost is implementation complexity and performance bounds stated only as asymptotic round complexity under graph-class and degree-concentration assumptions, not deployable ML infrastructure. It can fail outside the assumed strongly connected directed radio-network setting, polynomial identifier range, collision model, and degree-concentration conditions, and the unrestricted general case remains open. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: Auditing Conformal Prediction for Language Models Under Inference-Time Model Shift
item.description: This replaces the standard matched-protocol conformal evaluation where calibration and deployment share identical inference configurations. It requires running conformal calibration separately for each target deployment configuration (quantization mode, temperature) rather than reusing a single calibration set, increasing validation compute and complexity. Coverage guarantees fail silently if the deployed inference configuration differs from the calibration configuration, producing prediction sets that are systematically over-confident or under-confident relative to the nominal coverage rate. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: adopt.

item.title: Is 2:4 Sparsity Still Worth It? Semi-Structured Sparsity versus Quantization in LLM Inference
item.description: The technique replaces dense low-precision (e.g., FP8) linear layers with 2:4 semi-structured sparsity composed with that same low precision. It costs a mandatory retraining phase to recover model quality—perplexity recovers faster than reasoning ability—and introduces sparsity metadata overhead. It fails when a lower precision tier is still available (where dropping precision is both more accurate and faster) and on Blackwell hardware, where the required retraining budget did not recover the accuracy loss from the pairwise 4:8 pattern. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: sparsity and pruning. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Transformers as Generic Deep Neural Networks: Exact Compilation, the Cost of Removing Activation-Activation Products, and Multi-Agent Attention Clustering
item.description: The method replaces Transformer-specific NPU operators and Transformer-specific quantization pipelines with an exact compilation of attention, LayerNorm, and GELU MLP into generic affine, routing, square, sigmoid, and inverse-square-root primitives, plus an optional top-k attention scheme where centroid clustering reduces computed scores from N^2 to Nk per head. The cost is implementation complexity: exact compilation requires an elementwise activation-activation product to avoid an N^2 blowup in scalar nonlinear evaluations, and the top-k gains depend on centroid-based key preselection and tail-mass estimation rather than standard dense attention. It can fail when the target hardware lacks the required elementwise product or sigmoid and inverse-square-root operators, when query or agent clustering is weak so centroid key selection misses relevant keys, or when tail scores are not exchangeable, which breaks the unbiasedness guarantee and reintroduces the conditional bias of tail dropping. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: attention and kernels. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Local and Sparse Kernel Operator Learning for Incompressible Flows: An Operator Lagrange Formulation
item.description: The method replaces global output reconstruction and dense operator regression with local divergence-free interpolants solved in parallel on GPUs and sparse operator regression using compactly supported kernels. It requires one sparse solve per new input and fits the kernel support radius to data to control sparsity, though local coefficients are never explicitly formed. Validation depends on careful selection of sparsity patterns and support radii; performance degrades if the kernel support is misfitted or if the flow regime lacks sufficient local training data. 2 independent implementations, 1 star. Research area: other. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: MoEZip: Routing-Aware KV Cache Compression for Sparse Mixture-of-Experts LLMs
item.description: MoEZip replaces routing-agnostic KV eviction methods (e.g., attention-score-only policies) with a scoring system that combines attention weights and a Fisher-information metric of routing sensitivity, so eviction preserves expert selection during generation. The cost is additional per-token scoring computation, implementation complexity beyond standard eviction policies, and applicability restricted to sparse MoE architectures rather than dense models. It can fail if the Fisher-based sensitivity estimate does not transfer to a given MoE model or task, if the serving stack does not expose per-layer routing distributions needed to compute the metric, or if retention ratios below the evaluated regime degrade quality sharply. 1 independent implementation, 4 stars. Research area: KV cache. Recommendation: test.

item.title: A Quadratic Lens on Muon's Polar Update: Benefits, Pitfalls, and the Role of Newton-Schulz
item.description: The paper does not propose a replacement method; it analyzes the PolarGD orthogonalization inside Muon, showing it acts as iterate-dependent preconditioning whose speed depends on the conditioning of the iterate rather than the Hessian. The practical cost implication is that the Newton-Schulz iterations in Muon are not merely an approximation to be maximized: fewer iterations treat tiny singular values like gradient descent and can converge faster than exact orthogonalization. The identified failure mode is a slow regime where the iterate has tiny singular values, making PolarGD much slower than gradient descent; in a transformer trained with Muon, about a quarter of attention-matrix singular values fall in this regime. 0 independent implementations, 4 stars. Research area: efficient training. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: GAV: A scientific experimentation environment for PDE agents
item.description: Replaces fixed benchmark datasets and expensive numerical reference computations with a generative model of reference solutions that constructs verifiable PDE problems via the method of manufactured solutions. Costs include training a generator on simulation or experimental data and maintaining a closed-loop agent-verification pipeline, which increases system complexity and requires domain-specific validation data. Can fail if the generator learns a distribution that does not cover target physical regimes, produces solutions that permit trivial or non-representative problems, or if the verification metric poorly correlates with actual solver performance on downstream tasks. 2 independent implementations, 14 stars. Research area: coding agents. Recommendation: test.

item.title: EgoHand: Monocular 3D Hand Reconstruction from Egocentric Video
item.description: EgoHand replaces prior monocular egocentric hand-reconstruction pipelines (e.g., Apple EgoDex, Ropedia Xperience-10M) with a single transformer model over 2D hand crops using the SOMA-Hand parametric representation, released under a license permitting commercial use. Adoption costs the engineering effort of integrating a specialized vision model whose training required a 14-million-image curated corpus, though inference itself is cheap at roughly 9.69 ms per frame on standard hardware. It can fail on egocentric domains outside its training distribution, under occlusion or unusual camera intrinsics, and provides no value if the reader's production workload does not involve egocentric hand tracking. 1 independent implementation, 4 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: The Customer Is the Builder: How AI Coding Agents Are Rewriting the Economics of Software
item.description: This is a market and economics analysis, not an engineering technique: it examines whether organizations should replace purchased commercial software with functionality built in-house using AI coding agents. Adopting the paper's underlying premise costs engineering time for specification, validation, and ongoing maintenance of self-built tools, plus the reliability risk of early-stage generated code, none of which the paper prices concretely. What can fail: self-built substitutes may not meet acceptable quality or reliability standards, the benchmark extrapolation is not a forecast of real switching behavior, and market indicators currently show purchased software still growing. 2 independent implementations, 4 stars. Research area: coding agents. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: TerraTransfer++: Demonstration-Free End-to-End Planner
item.description: The method replaces imitation learning on curated expert driving logs with a self-play policy pretrained in a vectorized simulator, distilled via flow matching and adapter-based students on a frozen vision backbone, requiring only paired image/scene-state frames rather than demonstrations. The cost is substantial: it presupposes access to a high-throughput vectorized driving simulator, a pretrained vision backbone, photorealistic closed-loop evaluation infrastructure (3D Gaussian splatting), and multi-stage distillation with custom losses, all outside a 24 GB GPU budget and a small team's typical autonomous-driving scope. It can fail through sim-to-real gap: a policy whose entire supervision traces to simulator self-play may encode simulator-specific dynamics, and benchmark gains on HUGSim/NAVSIM do not establish on-road safety. 5 independent implementations, 171 stars. Research area: distillation. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Spike-Aware Gradient-Based Mixed-Precision Quantization of Spiking Neural Networks for Vision Applications
item.description: Replaces Hessian-based mixed-precision bit allocation (e.g., HAWQ-V2) for spiking neural networks with first-order gradient information, avoiding costly second-order computation over temporally unrolled timesteps. The cost is a quantization-specific search and calibration pipeline plus mixed-precision deployment support, which standard inference hardware handles poorly without custom kernels. It can fail for the reader because the method applies only to SNN workloads: on conventional ANN/LLM serving there is no benefit, and mixed bit-widths often yield no real speed or energy gain on commodity GPUs without specialized dataflow hardware. 3 independent implementations, 4 stars. Research area: quantization. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Climbing the Ladder: Automating Data Pipelines and Reproducing Baselines in Low-Resource Settings
item.description: The method replaces training small NMT models from scratch and manual data-pipeline scripting by porting tokenization and segmentation to maintained software, automating PDF sentence alignment with a language-agnostic encoder, and applying low-rank adapters to a pretrained multilingual model with staged training on forward-scored back-translations. It costs the memory and latency of loading the NLLB base model plus adapter overhead, requires curated parallel text and back-translation scoring infrastructure, and adds complexity in pipeline automation and threshold tuning. Multilingual adapters degrade directions they were not trained on, and performance varies by language pair, so gains are not uniform across all directions. 1 independent implementation, 126 stars. Research area: efficient training. Recommendation: adopt.

item.title: MemPlan: Memory-Conditioned PDDL Planning for Partially Observable Text Environments
item.description: The method replaces direct LLM-based action generation (e.g., ReAct) with a constrained LLM interface that parses observations into PDDL facts for a classical planner, reducing online inference costs. It requires offline supervised fine-tuning to train the language-to-symbol interface, adding training complexity and engineering effort for schema design. Performance may degrade if the parser hallucinates facts, if the PDDL domain becomes outdated, or if the environment dynamics exceed the representational capacity of the fixed symbolic model. 1 independent implementation, 126 stars. Research area: planning and decomposition. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Agent Mosaic: Recognizing Confidentiality Leaks in Agentic LLM Systems
item.description: Replaces ad hoc red-teaming with a documented risk case for inference-assembled confidentiality leaks. Costs are modest: threat-modeling time and restricted inference controls. It can fail because safeguards reduce disclosure but leaks persist even at 32.37% across all intents. 2 independent implementations, 14 stars. Research area: safety and guardrails. Recommendation: adopt.

item.title: Secure Agentic AI and Multimodal Intelligence in 6G Communication Systems
item.description: It replaces conventional AI and perimeter network security models with a cross-layer taxonomy for agentic perception, memory, tool use, communication, and orchestration. It costs survey-level integration effort rather than a deployable runtime method, with added complexity across prompt, memory, trust, orchestration, and privacy-preserving learning controls. It can fail if mitigations are treated as complete, if defenses do not transfer beyond 6G assumptions, or if attacks propagate through multimodal inputs, shared memory, tools, or inter-agent loops. 1 independent implementation, 14 stars. Research area: safety and guardrails. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Flow-based Spectral Kernel Learning for Nonstationary Attention
item.description: FSKA replaces fixed or stationary kernelized attention (and standard query-key projection attention) with a learned nonstationary spectral kernel parameterized by normalizing flows, eliminating query--key projections and using fixed orthogonal value projections. Costs include the added complexity of normalizing-flow spectral density estimation, potential instability in learning spectral densities, and the implementation overhead of a custom linear-attention kernel. After adoption, the flow-based spectral density may fail to regularize properly on out-of-distribution sequence lengths or tasks, the orthogonal value projection constraint may degrade representational capacity for certain modalities, and the 40%--47% parameter reduction may not translate to end-to-end latency gains if flow computation becomes the bottleneck. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: attention and kernels. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Rethinking SAE Evaluation: An Atomic Interpretable Unit Framework Reveals Hidden Polysemanticity and Redundancy
item.description: The framework replaces ad hoc SAE evaluation metrics (sparsity, dead-feature rate, reconstruction fidelity, monosemanticity checks) with a formalized objective—features should form an atomic interpretable unit basis—operationalized through dominance-aware proxy metrics such as DAME. It costs only additional evaluation computation on existing SAEs and models, requiring no retraining, but adopting the benchmarking suite adds integration and interpretation overhead for a small team. It can fail if proxy metrics do not correspond to downstream attribution or intervention usefulness, and the finding that dominant features are less interpretable and more redundant means SAEs passing conventional checks may still mislead circuit tracing or steering interventions. 2 independent implementations, 4 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: test.

item.title: FIGFLEX: A Mixed-Precision FP-INT GEMM Accelerator Co-Designed with Low-Bit LLM Quantization
item.description: FIGFLEX replaces GPU dequantize-to-FP16 tensor-core execution of weight-only quantized models with a custom bit-parallel FP-INT accelerator whose throughput scales as weight precision falls, paired with a mixed-precision quantizer that assigns per-group bit-widths. The approach requires non-commercial accelerator hardware (an ASIC/FPGA-class design), so adopting the performance gains is impossible on a 24 GB GPU or API-based setup; only the quantizer is potentially portable, at the cost of added quantization complexity. Without the custom datapath, the claimed throughput scaling does not materialize, and the accuracy results depend on the co-designed scaling scheme that has been validated only on LLaMA-2-7B WikiText-2. 0 independent implementations, 4 stars. Research area: quantization. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: What the Trace Shows and What the Label Says: Auditing Behavioral Detectors in Agent Evaluation
item.description: The practice replaces unqualified trace-level metrics (final correctness, re-verification, fault propagation) with labels accompanied by the underlying trace evidence, applicability flags, execution-limit status, and human corrections, exposed in a trace viewer. It costs engineering effort to instrument detectors and a viewer, plus storage and review overhead, with negligible inference cost since it operates on existing traces. It can fail if detector parsers disagree with human judgment in unanticipated patterns (the paper found 14 verification disagreements in four recurring classes), or if reported comparisons ignore step/token budgets, which the ablation shows can swing results by up to 6 of 30 problems. 3 independent implementations, 14 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: adopt.

item.title: Can LLMs Improve Their Own Harness? A Controlled Study on ARC-AGI-3
item.description: The method replaces human engineering of the symbolic harness (perception, memory, tool use, recovery, inference allocation) with frontier-model-generated code that the model revises twice, evaluated on held-out ARC-AGI-3 games. It costs full frontier-model inference for harness construction plus two revision cycles across 27 lineages, with dollar-denominated inference cost tracked as a resource measure; no GPU training is required, but the API spend is nontrivial. Self-revisions can fail to generalize (held-out gains are near zero and within noise), can regress existing capabilities, and human-steered harnesses retain substantial headroom. 2 independent implementations, 6 stars. Research area: coding agents. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: PLE: Physical-Engineering's Last Exam
item.description: PLE replaces saturated knowledge-based and toy engineering benchmarks with 85 long-horizon, agentic tasks that require completing realistic, billable engineering deliverables across electrical, civil, structural, and mechanical domains. It costs significant evaluation resources, as the top configuration spends 27M tokens and 63 minutes per task on average, making it expensive for routine iteration. It can fail to provide a stable signal for incremental product improvements because the tasks are extremely difficult, with even frontier models scoring only 50.6%. 3 independent implementations, 138 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Governed Self-Evolution for Autonomous Investing: A Multi-Agent LLM System with an Invariant Core
item.description: The method replaces a single general-purpose LLM making trading decisions with nine role-specialised agents (four analysts, a portfolio manager, a protected risk manager), a seven-layer shared memory assembled from the system's own record, and a nightly grading plus quarterly reflection loop gated by deterministic, reversible prompt edits around an untouchable core of order arithmetic and risk rules. The cost is substantial architectural complexity: nine agent roles, seven memory layers, a nightly grading pipeline, a quarterly reflector with replay verification, and roughly 1,632 LLM calls over 102 trading days (about 16 calls per day, feasible on third-party APIs but with ongoing per-call spend). Failure modes include prompt injections embedded in untrusted Web content (tested but only within one deployment), graded self-improvement loops that reinforce their own scoring biases, replay verification that cannot cover live-market distribution shift, and single-system live results that may not generalise across market regimes. 3 independent implementations, 1809 stars. Research area: multi-agent orchestration. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Stale Instruction Files Override the Code in Coding Agents: A One-Sentence Fix
item.description: The technique replaces the default behavior in which a project instruction file overrides conflicting existing code by adding one user-level instruction sentence that gives the existing code precedence. It costs one additional sentence in the user-level instruction file, with no reported memory, latency, or infrastructure cost, though the paper does not assess effects on tasks where following the instruction file would be correct. It can fail if the sentence is omitted, overridden by higher-priority instructions, or if agents or models change how they rank instruction sources. 1 independent implementation, 7 stars. Research area: coding agents. Recommendation: adopt.

item.title: What the Specification Did Not Say: Specification-Oracle Gaps in Test-Graded Coding-Agent Benchmarks
item.description: The method replaces blind trust in test-graded coding-agent benchmark scores with a static audit that flags tests depending on names, paths, or literals absent from the task specification, so benchmark results measure agent capability rather than recall of upstream implementation details. It costs an additional analysis pass over benchmark tasks (audit precision 89.2%, recall 92.9% held out) and adds tooling complexity without improving any agent's performance. It can fail by misclassifying dependencies in roughly 8-11% of cases, by not transferring to benchmarks whose construction it was not validated on, and by being unnecessary if the reader's evaluation tasks are already written or screened for their tests. 4 independent implementations, 136 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Governance-State Corruption in Long-Term Memory for LLM Agents: A Cross-Model Stress Test
item.description: This replaces evaluation of long-term memory solely by retrieval accuracy with an additional control-plane check that verifies validity-state enforcement over which records reach model context. It costs an offline auditing harness and matched fault-pair construction on existing benchmarks, with no added inference latency or model changes. It can fail silently in production if the memory layer lacks deterministic state enforcement, since retrieval can be correct while the operative context is wrong, and the frozen-scorer effects remain descriptive rather than validated semantic measures. 2 independent implementations, 14 stars. Research area: memory and context. Recommendation: test.

item.title: AgentTriage: Replayable Security Diagnosis Across Heterogeneous Agent Runtimes
item.description: Replaces ad hoc, LLM-judged forensic analysis of agent security events with a deterministic pipeline that normalizes heterogeneous runtime traces into a typed provenance graph and binds each diagnostic claim to recorded evidence, with mandatory abstention when evidence is missing. Costs include building and maintaining per-runtime overlays, enforcing a pre-run policy oracle, and instrumenting execution so invocation and result lifecycles are captured, which adds engineering complexity rather than GPU or inference cost. It can fail when runtime instrumentation is incomplete or identifiers cannot be reconciled, forcing abstention, and its replayability guarantees hold only for the five supported runtimes and pinned overlay versions, so unsupported or evolving runtimes may silently lose coverage. 3 independent implementations, 21 stars. Research area: safety and guardrails. Recommendation: test.

item.title: UniGuard: Multi-View Guardrail Learning for Cross-Interface Safety Generalization
item.description: UniGuard replaces interface-specific guardrail training (fixed prompt/response formats) with multi-view training over semantically aligned prompt, conversation, agent-trace, and multi-agent representations of the same safety case, using classification, contrastive, and calibration losses. The cost is a fine-tuning run on a 0.6B model (feasible on a single 24 GB GPU) plus constructing or adopting multi-view training data; inference cost remains that of a small classifier. It can fail because the 1,000-case synthetic dataset is small, gains are reported against its own pretrained baseline rather than standard production guardrails, and synthetic multi-view transformations may not capture real agent-trace distributions in the reader's deployment. 3 independent implementations, 1906 stars. Research area: safety and guardrails. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Is Complex Agentic Memory Always Needed? Naive RAG Is Stronger Than We Thought
item.description: The method replaces complex agentic memory pipelines involving mutation, structural organization, and learned retrieval with dense retrieval and reranking directly over raw conversation history. Its cost is the standard retrieval and reranking infrastructure plus a reader LLM call, avoiding the engineering and maintenance burden of memory transformation pipelines. Failure modes include degraded performance when retrieval misses necessary evidence, poor scaling to extremely long histories within a fixed context window, and domain shift where reranking quality drops. 5 independent implementations, 152 stars. Research area: retrieval and RAG. Recommendation: adopt.

item.title: AgentDP: Towards Automated Model Deployment for Heterogeneous Embedded AI Applications
item.description: AgentDP replaces the manual process of optimizing and adapting pre-trained AI models for heterogeneous embedded devices by using LLM agents to automate requirement elicitation, operator-aware model partitioning, and hyperparameter configuration reuse. The approach introduces dependency on LLM inference costs and requires integration of device-specific domain knowledge into the agent workflow, adding architectural complexity to the deployment pipeline. Failures can occur when the user requirement standardization misinterprets deployment constraints, when operator-aware partitioning selects incompatible execution engines, or when reused configurations from previous tasks do not transfer to new optimization targets. 2 independent implementations, 136 stars. Research area: coding agents. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: LLM Multi-Agent Systems Are Vulnerable to Herding and Runaway Cascades
item.description: This work replaces the assumption that aggregating multiple LLM agents reliably improves collective accuracy by demonstrating that social influence creates herding vulnerabilities analogous to human groups but with reduced self-correction. Implementing safeguards requires architectural changes such as limiting visibility into peer choices, restructuring information flow, or introducing diversity-preserving mechanisms, which adds system complexity and may reduce the coordination benefits of multi-agent setups. The primary failure mode is runaway cascades where agents converge on suboptimal outcomes amplified by feedback loops, particularly when agents can observe cumulative recommendation counts. 3 independent implementations, 136 stars. Research area: multi-agent orchestration. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Agentic Knowledge-Model Co-Evolution via Consistency Regularization
item.description: This technique replaces single-view experience analysis with a multi-view consistency check, where knowledge candidates are only adopted if they provide utility gains across different perturbations of the same experience. It requires significant infrastructure to support interleaved cycles of self-distillation and reinforcement learning, which increases computational cost and engineering complexity. Adoption can fail if the consistency regularization filters out necessary domain-specific nuances or if the overhead of maintaining multiple evolution views exceeds the available performance budget. 1 independent implementation, 132 stars. Research area: efficient training. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: REGATTA: A Cross-Domain Measurement Framework and Fault-Injection Harness for Enterprise AI Agents
item.description: REGATTA replaces ad hoc agent test suites and unverified compliance checklists with a source-cited checklist, a 25-fault injection corpus, and a two-stage harness that scores whether suites actually detect specified faults. Cost is limited to API-based LLM generation and judging plus the effort of auditing checklist citations against binding sources, all feasible on a small team without GPUs. What can fail: the audit found most checklist items misstated rules or had defective citations, stage agreement fell below chance (.536 vs .549) on a current-model retest, and substance review was partly AI-only, so adopted suites may embed wrong reference rules. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: test.

item.title: ReflectPO: Reflection-Guided Policy Optimization for Long-Horizon LLM Agents
item.description: ReflectPO replaces standard RL fine-tuning of tool-use agents (e.g., trajectory-level reward methods) with reflection-guided sampling and tree-structured action-level credit assignment using parent-child reward differences and recovery gains. It costs a full RL training pipeline with tree-organized trajectory sampling, environment branching, and reward instrumentation, which is infeasible on a single 24 GB GPU or API-only access without dedicated training infrastructure and budget. It can fail if reward signals are sparse or mis-specified, if hint construction from branch differences does not generalize to the reader's domain, or if the improved error-recovery behavior does not transfer to different tool environments. 4 independent implementations, 152 stars. Research area: failure recovery. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Repair Changes Which Layers to Remove: Exact Optima for Depth Pruning of Language Models
item.description: The method replaces heuristic, repair-agnostic layer-removal scores (as in SLEB and ReplaceMe) with a greedy search that selects layers under the linear repair that will actually be applied, plus a second-order loss score that identifies the repaired block from one forward and one backward pass of the intact model. Costs are modest: no retraining, but the greedy search requires repeated evaluations of pruned-and-repaired variants (the paper itself ran roughly 53,000 evaluations for the exact study), and the linear repair map must be computed per removal block. It can fail when the optimal pruned layout differs sharply across model families or downstream tasks, when the linear repair poorly approximates removed-layer interactions for non-contiguous removals, and when perplexity gains do not transfer to the reader's specific task metrics. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: sparsity and pruning. Recommendation: test.

item.title: From Clinical Judgment to Checkable Rules: Clinician-Led Guardrails for Mental-Health Chatbots
item.description: Replaces prompt engineering, LLM-as-a-Judge, and Constitutional AI safety evaluation with a clinician-authored, formally verified four-rule base applied as a guardrail whose every verdict is recomputable from sixteen named facts. Costs: clinician time to define and adjudicate rules, a fact-extraction step, and a measured over-refusal regression where a specification revision raised block-class outcomes on held-out boundary prompts from 6.0% to 16.0%, plus an uncertainty default that can over-block. Can fail when fact extraction misidentifies content (the main source of the over-refusal regression) and when the fixed rule set misses safety failures outside its four checks, where the LLM judge may remain stronger. 1 independent implementation, 10 stars. Research area: safety and guardrails. Recommendation: adopt.

item.title: Primal-Dual Representation Learning for Low-Rank Constrained MDPs
item.description: This replaces tabular or representation-agnostic constrained-MDP algorithms with a method that learns low-rank transition features via maximum likelihood and plans under optimistic Lagrangian or lower-confidence-certificate objectives. It costs an explicit feature-learning exploration phase (decaying epsilon-greedy mixture execution), which inflates sample complexity to O(K^3/4) when exploratory actions are charged, plus nontrivial implementation of uncertainty bonuses and stabilized dual search. It can fail outside its assumptions: the guarantees depend on the low-rank transition structure holding, on known feature dimensionality, and on an online episodic interaction setting that does not match typical offline or single-deployment production problems. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Gandalf: Flash Shall Not Die! Increasing Flash Storage Lifetime for KV Cache Offloading in LLM Serving
item.description: Gandalf replaces naive or purely access-pattern-based admission policies for writing KV caches to SSD, instead gating admission using application-level signals such as attention type, prioritizing full-attention KV entries. It costs implementation complexity in the serving stack, requires an SSD offloading tier and workloads (multi-round conversation, agents) with KV write volumes large enough to threaten SSD endurance, and assumes attention type predicts future reuse. It can fail if the serving engine lacks SSD offloading entirely, if workload write volume never approaches SSD endurance limits (making the optimization irrelevant), or if the access-pattern/hit-rate tradeoff shifts under attention architectures or traces unlike those evaluated. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: KV cache. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Amplifying Latency and Cost of LLM Inference via Rowhammer Attack
item.description: LLVMhammer replaces nothing in the reader's stack; it is an attack that flips a DRAM bit in Triton's target-independent compilation pipeline so the compiler emits a functionally identical but slower GPU kernel, which then persists via Triton's on-disk kernel cache. There is no adoption cost because it is not a capability; the relevant defensive cost is operational: ECC memory, integrity checks or cache invalidation for compiled kernels, and restricting untrusted code co-residency on inference hosts. The attack itself can fail against ECC-equipped hardware, and defenses can fail if kernel caches are trusted blindly or if third-party API infrastructure (outside the reader's control) is the actual exposure point. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: safety and guardrails. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Neural Spectral Capacity with Residual Context for Heterogeneous Resource Allocation within Transformers
item.description: ResNSC replaces position-independent per-layer spectral capacity scoring (NSC) and its dynamic-programming width allocator with a residual-history-aware scoring function that jointly allocates residual and feed-forward widths under a parameter budget, requiring no training data or instantiated weights for evaluation. The cost is implementation complexity: the scoring and augmented DP allocator must be integrated into an architecture-selection or pruning pipeline, and the method only ranks candidates, so actual training or fine-tuning is still required to realize gains. It can fail if the statistical residual-state assumptions do not hold for the target architecture family, if the finite candidate set excludes the true optimum, or if perplexity/task gains at 121M-374M and LLaMA-7B pruning do not transfer to the reader's models and budgets. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: efficient architectures. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Low-Latency MoE Inference in Space Data Centers: A Wireless-Power-Transfer Perspective
item.description: The method replaces passive, per-satellite solar power allocation in orbital data centers with laser-based wireless power transfer that redistributes harvested energy from idle to active MoE experts, controlled by a two-sided water-filling policy. It costs inter-satellite WPT hardware, incurs transfer losses, and adds a power-routing control layer, with benefits bounded by link efficiency and formation geometry. It can fail or yield no gain when WPT efficiency is low, expert activation is balanced, or the infrastructure does not exist. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: OpenAttention: One Percent Is Enough with Tail Proxies
item.description: Replaces dense attention over the full KV cache with top-k key selection plus a count-aware mean proxy token that folds in the unread tail, using training-free query-geometry clustering, error-based read allocation (ErrorGate), and a custom flash kernel.
